ruleName: Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

Long-form policy article: an inline glossary-term tooltip (Emissions Trading System) opens downward on hover/focus with no Esc dismiss, landing on the first ~3 lines of the next body paragraph. Method 2 absent, so Method 1 is the only path — and it obscures meaningful body text.

Healthcare patient-portal blood-pressure intake. Side-by-side Systolic (value 118, normal) and Diastolic (value 135, out of range) number inputs. The error 'Diastolic must be between 40 and 120 mmHg.' is placed in the Systolic column under the Systolic input, and the Systolic input carries the red alert border; the out-of-range Diastolic has no message. No aria-describedby.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the problem by instructing the user to remove letters and parentheses from a value that consists purely of digits.

ruleName: CONTROL / discrimination foil (PASS). Event-ticketing phone field, post-submit error state — near-identical component to case-01. The retained value is '(202) 555-CALL', which genuinely contains parentheses, a space, a dash, and the letters C-A-L-L. The field is digits-only and the visible associated error reads 'Phone number must contain only digits. Remove the letters, spaces, and parentheses (for example, enter 2025550143).' — a cause that DID occur and correctly describes this value's actual defect.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is clearly identified in text describing the specific format violation for the mobile number field.

ruleName: RTL Arabic (lang=ar dir=rtl) membership address form. A 2-column x 3-row CSS grid holds Postal code (column 1, value 11564, flagged red) and City (column 2, empty). The postal-code error is placed by explicit coordinates into grid-column 2 row 3 — the City column's message slot — so on screen it sits under the empty City input. No aria-describedby.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message fails 3.3.1 because it contradicts the 5-digit value ('11564') actually retained in the flagged postal code field.
No error was triggered or demonstrated for the city input field.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): auction 'place a bid' form with the IDENTICAL red border + tint on the email field, but the error is also identified and described in text ('Email address is not valid.') tied via aria-describedby, with aria-invalid='true' and the decorative icon aria-hidden. Should pass.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated for the 'Your name' input field.
The error on the email field is clearly identified in text and programmatically associated.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the maximum bid field.

ruleName: Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

Retail account signup re-displayed after a failed submit; the email field holds a malformed address (jane.summit.example.com, no @) and the sole per-field error indicator is an error icon carrying a non-empty but uselessly generic alt="error".

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input is not in an error state or flagged as invalid, so error identification does not apply to this element.
The input error is indicated only by visual styling and a generic icon with the alt text 'error', with no textual explanation of the problem.
No error was demonstrated for the password field because only the email address field was flagged with an error.

ruleName: SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

Bank reset-password screen redisplayed after rejecting a reused password; the field shows a red outline + a red CSS ::before key glyph and carries aria-invalid='true', but emits NO error text, aria-errormessage, or aria-describedby — nothing in words states what is wrong or why.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is indicated solely through visual styling and aria-invalid without any descriptive text identifying the error.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the 'Confirm new password' field.

ruleName: Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

Alumni reunion RSVP (en-GB); email ravi@@pembury.ac.uk (double @) and date 2024-07-18 (in the past) are both invalid, but a refactor cut-and-pasted the date row's error icon above the email row without updating it, so the email field sits beside an SVG whose aria-label="Date is in the past" — correct cause for the wrong field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Full name input field, so error identification is not applicable.
The error for the email address field is not identified in text, providing only visual red-border/icon cues and an incorrect aria-label describing a date error.
The invalid 'Preferred dinner date' field is indicated solely through visual styling and an aria-invalid attribute without any text identifying or describing the error.

ruleName: PASSING counter-fixture. Higher-ed LMS reading with a '[1]' footnote reference that opens a citation popup on hover AND keyboard focus, deliberately overlapping the paragraph below (so Method 1 is not relied on). A document-level Escape handler hides the popup while focus REMAINS on the '[1]' button, and activating the trigger also toggles it closed — both SCR39-allowed dismissals.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The additional content revealed on hover remains persistently visible while the trigger is hovered and does not self-withdraw on a timer.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is hovered.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): the same Riverbend Library membership flow as case-01, but the genuine SUCCESS result after VALID input (Age 34, a real email). The server accepted the data and rendered a true confirmation — a read-only summary of the accepted values, a real membership number (RVB-2026-08831), and next steps — with no editable form re-displayed and legitimately no error message. Must be judged passed while case-01..05 are failed.

E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

Cedar Mutual Auto 3-step quote wizard silently advanced to 'Step 3 of 3, Review & buy' after an invalid ZIP ('0', too short) on Step 1 was swallowed — Step 2 (coverage options) was skipped because the rating engine had no usable ZIP. The review summary freezes the invalid ZIP '0' as read-only text and shows a placeholder premium '$—'; no error text appears. Cross-page silent-advance variant. LONG-TAIL; content-domain insurance quote wizard, APG stepper + dl review, lazy-validation persona.

SaaS 'set your password' screen, post-submit error state. Password field holds a 12-character value (shown as 12 bullets); the visible associated error reads 'Password must be at least 8 characters.' The page's own requirements checklist marks 'At least 8 characters' as MET (green) and 'At least one number' as the only UNMET rule (red). The error asserts a length rule already passed; the actual unmet rule (digit) triggered rejection but is not the one described, so the error contradicts the page's own checklist.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The form displays an incorrect error message that contradicts the actual input value and fails to identify the real validation error.

ruleName: Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

Healthcare new-patient intake form: a 'What's this?' help popover on the Insurance Member ID field opens down-right with no Esc dismiss and overlaps the next field's required asterisk + label (Patient date of birth) and the input being filled.

GOV.UK council-tax reduction form: top-of-form red error summary announces 'We found 2 errors' and lists Full name + Email, but both render filled and unflagged; the only field actually in error (Telephone, value 'ring me weekdays') has a red border, inline message and aria-invalid=true and is never named. Wrong count AND wrong fields named.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary incorrectly identifies the Full name field as being in error when it is not flagged or invalid on the form.
The error summary block misidentifies form errors by reporting failures for full name and email while completely omitting the telephone number field that is actually flagged in error.

ruleName: BOUNDARY PASS. Community-garden waitlist form with stacked Full name (valid), Email (value 'priya.nair@', invalid), Phone (valid). The error 'Email address is incomplete — add the part after the @.' is rendered inside the Email field's own block directly under the Email input, which carries the red invalid border. There is NO aria-describedby — identification rests entirely on presentation, done correctly.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Full name field.
The error for the email address field is clearly identified in text.
No error was triggered or flagged for the optional Phone field.

ruleName: Credit-union online-banking enrolment: red role=alert summary states 'Password must be at least 10 characters and include a number', but the Password field is valid (green, aria-invalid=false, meets the rule). The only flagged field is its sibling Confirm password (aria-invalid=true, red, 'does not match the password you entered'). The summary blames the wrong sibling and describes a different cause.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was detected or surfaced for the Username input field.
The error summary incorrectly identifies the Password field as invalid despite it meeting all stated requirements.
The error summary misidentifies what went wrong by reporting a password complexity error on the valid Password field while omitting the error on the Confirm password field.

ruleName: CONTROL (passing): flight-booking Passenger details step. Red role=alert summary states 'There are 2 problems' and lists exactly two G139 jump links — Email (→#email) and Date of birth (→#dob). The page flags exactly those two fields with matching aria-invalid, anchors, and inline message wording; the two valid fields (Given names, Passport number) are correctly not mentioned. Count, membership, link targets, and wording all reconcile.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Given names field is not in error on this form, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.
The passport number field is not in an error state and was not rejected, so there is no error identification to evaluate.
The error for the email address field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.
The error for the Date of birth field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout payment row (Card number / Expiry / CVV) in a flex row. The CVV value '12' is the truly-invalid input, but the error 'CVV must be exactly 3 digits.' is rendered in the message slot under the Card number field, and the Card number input carries the red invalid border. No aria-describedby anywhere.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Card number field is flagged as invalid but displays an incorrect error message referencing the CVV instead.
The Expiry field is valid and unflagged, so error identification does not apply to this control.
The error message for the CVV field is incorrectly rendered and flagged under the Card number field rather than identifying the CVV input.

ruleName: Real-estate listing: the entire large Walk Score hero tile is the hover/focus trigger; its explainer popover is pushed away into the next column to avoid the trigger, but lands on the Monthly cost estimate breakdown. No Esc dismiss. Tests the large-trigger 'Method 2 only' nuance.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip obscures adjacent content and cannot be dismissed with Escape or without moving the pointer.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains visible when the pointer moves onto it.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists for as long as the trigger remains hovered without disappearing on an automatic timer.

ruleName: Nonprofit one-time-gift form; the donor entered 25000 (over the stated $10,000 online maximum) and the error is conveyed by a Material-Icons-style icon-font glyph whose aria-label is the literal ligature key "error_outline" — describing the picture, not the error.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The form field indicates an error using only visual styling and a generic icon without descriptive error text.
The target 'Name on card' input is not in an error state and was not flagged as invalid, so error identification does not apply to this field.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout shipping step, post-submit error state. ZIP field retains the value the user typed, '9021' (four digits). The visible associated server error reads 'ZIP code 90210 not found in our database. Please check the code and try again.' — quoting '90210', a five-digit value the user never entered (a normalizer padded a trailing zero before lookup). The real defect (ZIP too short) is never described and the quoted value contradicts the field's own retained value.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The target Street address field is not in an error state, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to it.
No error was demonstrated for the City input field, so error identification does not apply to this element.
The State field is not in an error state, so error identification does not apply to this control.
The error message misidentifies the error by stating that ZIP code 90210 was not found when the value actually entered in the field is 9021.

ruleName: Homeware ecommerce checkout (en-GB); shipping postcode 9021 is too short and billing postcode SW1A 0AA! has an illegal character, but both reuse one SVG sprite and both <svg role=img> wrappers carry the identical hardcoded aria-label="Invalid input".

rubricVerdicts.summary: The street address input was not flagged in error and is not rejected upon form submission.
The error on the postcode field is not identified in text, relying only on a red border and a warning icon with the generic label 'Invalid input'.
The billing street address field is not in an error state and was not flagged as invalid, so error identification does not apply.
The error on the billing postcode field is indicated only by a red outline and a generic 'Invalid input' icon without identifying what is wrong.

ruleName: E-commerce category sidebar: hovering a top-level category ("Camp & Hike") reveals a CSS-only flyout submenu offset to the right (left:230px against a 210px row, leaving a ~20px transparent corridor). The flyout is a DOM child of the category but not geometrically contiguous; reaching lower submenu items requires a diagonal down-and-right path that exits both hot-zones, ending the :hover state and collapsing the flyout before the cursor arrives.

Hotel booking review, post-submit error state. Check-in '2026-08-01', check-out '2026-09-25' (55 nights — check-out IS after check-in). The check-out field's visible associated error reads 'Check-out date must be after your check-in date.' — a relation that already holds. The form's own visible policy states 'Maximum stay: 30 nights'; the real, undescribed error is that a 55-night stay exceeds that cap.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The check-in input field is not flagged as invalid or in error, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification is not applicable to this element.
The error is misidentified because the error message claims the check-out date must be after the check-in date, which contradicts the valid chronological order of the entered dates.

ruleName: Restaurant catering-enquiry form: red role=alert summary lists three errors (Event date, City, Number of guests). Event date and Number of guests are genuinely flagged below, but the middle line 'City is required' names a field that does not exist anywhere on the form — the page collects a single free-text 'Venue name & full address' textarea with no City input, label, or control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error for the Event date field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.
The venue textarea field is valid and not in error, so error identification does not apply to this control.
The error for the Number of guests field is clearly identified in text both inline and in the error summary.

ruleName: Healthcare patient-intake form (step 1 of 3); an impossible date of birth (31/02/1991) is flagged ONLY by a red exclamation-triangle SVG image with alt='' beside the field. No nearby/hidden text, aria-label, or aria-invalid conveys the error.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Full name input field, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification is not applicable to this element.
The invalid date of birth input is flagged only by a visual warning icon without any textual error description.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Contact number field.
The Registered GP surgery field is not flagged in error, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.

ruleName: Conference call-for-papers form returned after a blank required 'Talk title'; the only error/required cue is the label turned red with a trailing CSS ::after asterisk. No message, no legend explaining the asterisk, no required/aria-required/aria-invalid.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was identified or flagged for the Full name field.
No error was flagged or surfaced for the Date of birth field, so there is no error identification to evaluate for this control.
The invalid postcode field is indicated only by a red border and icon without any text identifying or describing the error.
No error was surfaced or flagged for the vehicle registration field.

ruleName: Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. The reveal is the selector abbr.term:hover .bubble with no JS, so keyboard focus structurally cannot reveal it; the author also set tabindex="-1", removing the <abbr> from the tab order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom hover tooltip obscures underlying text and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any in-place mechanism while hovered.
The hover-revealed tooltip disappears when the pointer travels from the trigger toward the tooltip because a 10px gap separates them.
The tooltip content revealed on hover remains visible for the duration of the hover without dismissing itself.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field retains '03/14/2027', which already conforms exactly to MM/DD/YYYY. The visible associated error reads 'Date of birth is invalid. Please use the MM/DD/YYYY format.' — naming a constraint that is already satisfied. The actual error (a birth date set in the future) is never described, so the only guidance is a no-op fix.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was surfaced or flagged for the Legal name field, so error identification for this input is not applicable.
The error message misidentifies the error as an invalid format even though the field already conforms to the requested MM/DD/YYYY format.

ruleName: RTL Arabic e-commerce product page: a size-guide tooltip authored with physical left:0 does not mirror under dir=rtl and opens on top of its own trigger button, covering the label 'دليل المقاسات'. No Esc dismiss. Obscures the trigger itself — FAIL.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The delay reason tooltip triggered on focus/hover obscures page content and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key without moving focus.
The hover-triggered tooltip disappears as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger button to move onto the revealed content.
The hover/focus-triggered tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger element is held and does not disappear on a timer.

ruleName: Government SNAP-benefits two-column grid form. Row 1 has First name (left, filled 'Maria') and Last name (right, filled). After a failed submit the error 'First name is required.' is placed in the right-column cell directly under the Last name input, and Last name (not First name) gets aria-invalid=true. No aria-describedby links the message to any control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error is not correctly identified for the first name field because the error message 'First name is required.' is placed under and associated with the last name input instead of the first name input.
The error message displayed beneath the flagged Last name field incorrectly states 'First name is required.', failing to identify the error for this field.
No error was detected or asserted for the Middle initial field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Preferred name field.

ruleName: CONTROL (passes): government heating-assistance application; the email carla.mendes#state.gov uses # instead of @ and the error icon carries a correct, specific alt="Email address must contain an @ symbol — for example, name@example.com", echoed by a linked error summary.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error occurred or was flagged for the applicant name field.
The error for the email address field is clearly identified in text both in the error summary banner and via the icon text alternative associated with the control.
No error was detected or flagged for the Phone number field.

ruleName: Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The additional hover content remains persistent and does not disappear on its own while the trigger remains hovered or focused.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists for as long as the trigger remains hovered, without timing out or withdrawing on its own.

ruleName: Helios Energy kWh bar chart: each SVG rect bar has an SVG <title> child (UA-rendered native tooltip, e.g. 'February: 612 kWh', out of scope) AND an author .vtip floating overlay shown on hover with DIFFERENT, richer text ('Feb · 612 kWh · $84.10 · 18% below your 12-mo avg'). The overlay is pointer-events:none, repositions under the cursor via mousemove, and has no Escape handler. Two on-hover sources, two owners, two divergent texts — the reviewer must separate which content the SC governs (only the author overlay) and judge its behavior.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip content remains visible while the trigger is held and does not dismiss itself on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip directly overlaps the trigger bar with no physical gap, allowing pointer travel onto the revealed content.
The hover-triggered additional content remains visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists without self-withdrawing while the trigger remains hovered.
The hover-revealed tooltip directly overlaps the trigger element, allowing the pointer to move onto it without crossing any gap.
The hover-revealed additional content remains persistently visible for as long as the trigger is hovered without withdrawing itself on a timer.

ruleName: Online-banking add-payee; the German IBAN DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 0X ends in an illegal X and is invalid (red border), but a Vue state-merge bug left the field's status SVG at its initial success state: a green check with <title>Looks good!</title> — an inverted text alternative.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was detected or flagged for the Payee name input field, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.
The invalid IBAN field is marked with a red border and aria-invalid='true', but the error is not identified or described in text.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the optional reference field.

ruleName: Home-insurance quote wizard, step 2 Property: red role=alert summary says 'Please fix 2 things: Country must be selected. Year the property was built must be a 4-digit year'. Year built is genuinely flagged (value 'nineteen eighty'), but the Country control is a disabled <select> pre-set to 'United Kingdom' (locked because the product is UK-only) — greyed, non-focusable, no aria-invalid — and could not have produced input nor be corrected.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary falsely identifies an error on the disabled Country field that cannot be edited and is already pre-selected.
No error was triggered or demonstrated for the Property postcode input field.
The error for the year input field is clearly identified in text both inline and in the error summary.

ruleName: Folio & Thread e-commerce checkout (Step 3 of 3, Payment) bounced after the gateway rejected a 13-digit card number ('4716 1234 5678 9', too short) and empty CVC; the theme injected a green role=status banner 'Thank you — your order is being processed' above the re-displayed payment form with the invalid card retained. Variant B (mismatched success banner). HEAD-prevalence; content-domain e-commerce/checkout, Shopify-Dawn-style theme.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was triggered or displayed for this field, so error identification cannot be evaluated.
No input error was demonstrated or flagged for the card number field, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply.
No error was triggered or demonstrated for the expiry input field.

ruleName: City government primary nav: a 'Residents & Services' submenu opens on hover and on activation/focus of its toggle and covers the page banner and intro text. It carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls, but the only way it closes is a document-level click outside the menu (pointer only) — no Escape handler and activating the toggle only re-opens it, so keyboard/magnifier users cannot dismiss the obscuring panel without moving focus away.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Hovering or focusing the Government navigation link changes only its background styling and does not reveal any additional content.
Hovering over the 'Government' navigation link only changes its background styling and does not reveal any additional content.
The navigation element does not trigger additional hover content that withdraws itself while hovered.
No additional content or tooltip was triggered on hover or focus of the Business link to evaluate dismissability.
Hovering over the Business navigation item does not reveal any additional content.
The navigation link does not trigger any additional content on hover or focus, so no persistence barrier exists under WCAG 1.4.13.

ruleName: SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

ruleName: Community allotment newsletter signup re-rendered after a failed submit; the invalid email field ('tom@') wears a 2px red border + red-tinted background as the SOLE error cue. No message, no aria-invalid, no hidden text anywhere conveys that an error occurred.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated for the Name input field, as the form's error state pertains to a different field.
No error was detected or demonstrated for the 'Course you want to join' input field.
The rejected field is visually flagged with red styling but provides no text identifying or describing the error.

ruleName: University admissions application wizard, step 3 Contact details: red role=alert summary lists two G139-style jump links. Both fields (Email holding 'amara.k(at)mail', empty Telephone) are genuinely flagged, but the link labelled 'Fix your email address' has href=#phone, so activating it lands focus on the Telephone field instead of email; both links in fact point to #phone.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Preferred name field is not in an error state and was not rejected, so error identification does not apply to this control.
The error summary misdirects users by linking the email address error message to the daytime telephone input field instead of the email input field.
The error for the daytime telephone field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient registration: red role=alert summary declares 'There is 1 error in this form' and lists only Date of birth, but three fields render red with inline messages and aria-invalid=true — Date of birth (invalid date), Mobile number (too short), and Postcode (invalid). The summary undercounts the real error state by two and omits two flagged fields.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The First name field is valid and was not flagged or rejected with an error, so 3.3.1 does not apply to this element.
The error on the Date of birth field is accurately identified in text both inline and in the summary.
The mobile number input is marked in error but is omitted from the error summary alert, which incorrectly reports only a single error on the form.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Address line 1 input.
The form's error summary announces only one error and omits the invalid postcode field.

ruleName: Cedar Valley Health patient portal A1C trend chart: five hemoglobin A1C results are drawn as absolutely-positioned <div> markers; hovering reveals a popup with the exact value, date, and the provider's per-result clinical note (e.g. dose increased to 1000mg, recheck in 3 months). Those values and notes appear only in the hover popups (no data-table fallback). Markers are non-focusable <div>s with mouseenter/mouseleave-only popups, so keyboard users can read none of the data.

Aurora Transit trip planner: each leg has a round service-note icon where the author sets title='' to suppress the native tooltip, then paints an identical gray bubble with a pure-CSS ::after { content: attr(data-hint) } (no JavaScript). The bubble appears only while the 22px icon itself is :hovered; a ::after pseudo-element cannot receive the pointer and there is no Escape affordance. Indistinguishable from a native tooltip, but author CSS owns it, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

ruleName: French bistro reservation form re-rendered after no seating choice was made; the required radio group is flagged ONLY by reddening its <legend> ('Préférence de salle'). No text says a choice is required or that the group errored; no aria-required/aria-invalid.

ruleName: Government DMV registration-renewal wizard: focus-triggered help bubbles (role=tooltip) under the Plate and VIN fields. A single global setInterval(...,5000) clears any visible bubble every 5 seconds, so the VIN help vanishes while the field still has focus and the user is mid-task. Verified: visible on focus -> display:none at 6s while document.activeElement is still #vin.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus-revealed tooltip remains persistently visible while the input control retains focus without self-dismissing on a timer.

ruleName: Brightwater Rivers Trust donation page bounced after the amount was submitted as $0.00 (below the stated $5 minimum) AND the required 'How often?' frequency radio group was left unselected; a warm 'Thank you for your generosity' banner sits above the re-displayed form with the bad amount retained and the radio group still empty and unflagged. Variant B with a second omitted required field. MID/long-tail; content-domain nonprofit/donation, fieldset radio group + currency input, fundraising-CMS persona.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The invalid donation amount field is flagged at rest with a retained invalid value of 0.00, but no error message in text identifies the error.

No input error was demonstrated or flagged for this radio button field.

The email field does not provide any textual error identification when invalid input is provided.

ruleName: Northwind Pharmacy refill queue: each status help icon shipped with a native title=, but a Bootstrap/jQuery-UI-style tooltip plugin strips the native title on load (removeAttribute('title')) and renders its own gray span.nwtip styled to mimic the native UA tooltip. The author bubble is pointer-events:none, toggled only on mouseenter/mouseleave of the 18px icon, with no Escape handler. Visually near-identical to the case-01 native tooltip, but author-owned, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

ruleName: Arabic RTL airline seat-selection page: a held seat (C٢) shows, on hover/focus, a role=tooltip with the live remaining hold time (Arabic-Indic countdown). The popup stays visible the whole time the hold is valid and the seat is hovered; when the countdown reaches zero the hold genuinely expires (seat released, message now false) and the popup is removed because its information became invalid. Verified: visible through countdown ٠٠:٠٧ -> ٠٠:٠٤, removed only after real expiry, seat no longer held, pay button shows 'hold timed out'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip is not hoverable because moving the pointer off the trigger button onto the tooltip causes the tooltip to disappear.
The hover-revealed seat reservation message persists while hovered and clears only when the temporary hold expires and its information is no longer valid.

ruleName: Corporate intranet expense-claim editor; a £139 meal line breaching the £75 cap is flagged ONLY by a yellow-highlighted <fieldset> (the firm's 'highlight in yellow' convention) with the intended descriptive text omitted. No message, hidden text, or aria state.

ruleName: Fintech dashboard: an SVG line chart of daily NAV where each <circle> data point shows a detail pop-up on mouseenter, offset above-and-right of the point. Points are closely spaced (~26px) and share one reusable pop-up. To read the offset pop-up for a point under magnification, the pointer must travel toward it — crossing the next data point, whose mouseenter replaces the wanted pop-up with the neighbour's (the exact F95 chart example).
